answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust to a beacon of verifiable work: each identity must periodically publish a costly, checkable proof - a completed job attested by its counterparties - before it can trade. Like ships queuing at a wharf, newcomers wait in line and pay docking fees in compute, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs more than any fable of quick profit can justify; honest agents amortize that cost across many real transactions.
